name: JUSTICE WECHT
description: Concurred, argued that judges must curtail their First Amendment rights regarding partisan commentary while on the bench to maintain impartiality, distinguishing their speech from that of judicial candidates, but also noted that merely referencing past legislative deeds is not inherently transgressive if not done with a partisan tilt.

name: Wecht, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the average search engine user does not have an expectation of privacy in records generated by unprotected internet searches.

name: Chief Justice Todd
description: Concurred, argued that there was sufficient evidence of probable cause to support the issuance of the warrant.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Concurred, argued that sufficient probable cause existed for the warrant, making the constitutional privacy issue unnecessary to resolve, but noted agreement with the OAJC's view on privacy if it were necessary.

name: Stacy Wallace
description: Concurred, arguing that the Borough's Code provisions for administrative warrants without individualized probable cause violate the Pennsylvania Constitution's protection against unreasonable searches.

name: JUSTICE BROBSON
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court's order compelling arbitration does not meet the irreparability prong of the collateral order doctrine, as the propriety of the order can be reviewed on appeal after a final judgment, and the Pridgen case is inapplicable.

name: Justice McCaffery
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this matter.

name: WECHT, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Section 3755 is facially unconstitutional as it mandates warrantless searches without a recognized exception.

name: MUNDY, JUSTICE
description: Dissented, argued that Section 3755 is not facially unconstitutional because it can be applied constitutionally with a warrant or exigent circumstances, and that the immunity provision in Section 3755(b) should be upheld.

name: BROBSON, JUSTICE
description: Dissented, argued that Section 3755 is not facially unconstitutional because it can be applied constitutionally if law enforcement obtains a warrant or if exigent circumstances exist, and that the statute is directed at medical professionals.

name: JUSTICE DOUGHERTY
description: Concurred, argued that the Commonwealth Court erred in denying intervention to Nonprofits because they had a legally enforceable interest and DEP did not adequately represent them, and dismissed the preliminary injunction appeal as moot.

name: TODD, C.J.
description: Concurred, joined the majority opinion and Justice Donohue's concurring opinion.

name: DONOHUE
description: Concurred, joined the majority opinion and filed a separate concurring opinion.

name: MUNDY
description: Concurred and dissented, arguing the intervention order was not appealable and Nonprofits' interests were adequately represented, but agreed the preliminary injunction appeal was moot.

name: BROBSON
description: Concurred and dissented, arguing Nonprofits had no right to intervene and DEP adequately represented their interests, but agreed the preliminary injunction appeal was moot.

name: JUSTICE DONOHUE
description: Dissented, argued that the Commonwealth failed to establish a high-crime area with objective evidence and that the designation was irrelevant to establishing reasonable suspicion for Lewis's seizure, thus the evidence should be suppressed.

name: Dougherty, J.
description: Concurred with the majority opinion, affirming the lower court's decision to deny suppression.

name: Justice Wecht
description: Concurred, arguing that mere presence among a group engaged in criminal activity, like gambling, could establish reasonable suspicion for each member of the group.

name: JUSTICE WECHT
description: Concurred, argued that the court should use a traditional rational basis test under the Pennsylvania Constitution's Article I, Sections 1 and 11, rather than the 'Gambone test' which he views as judicial overstepping, and that state constitutional challenges should not be mischaracterized as 'due process' challenges.

name: JUSTICE BROBSON
description: Dissented, argued that the Majority misinterprets prior precedent (Genser) by applying it too broadly to all disqualified mail ballots, and that the Board's actions were consistent with the Election Code, and that the Majority's decision creates nonuniformity in election procedures.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Concurred, argued that the Uniform Firearms Act requires PSP to provide background check results as quickly as possible with available resources, making a good faith effort to staff the system to minimize response times, and that while injunctive and mandamus relief are barred by sovereign immunity, declaratory relief is available to clarify these duties.

name: Chief Justice Todd
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, arguing that declaratory relief, standing alone, may not provide practical good and that appellants might be underwhelmed by its effect.

name: DONOHUE JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Judge Braxton's simultaneous holding of judicial office and a prohibited position of profit created a constitutionally impermissible conflict of duties, making his judicial orders voidable, but rejected the automatic forfeiture rule applied by the Commonwealth Court.

name: MUNDY, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the error was structural but subject to waiver, and resulted in presumed prejudice, clarifying the majority's stance on 'structural error' terminology.

name: JUSTICE BROBSON
description: Concurred, argued that the state firearm preemption laws are constitutional and do not violate substantive due process, create a state-created danger, or improperly interfere with delegated public health duties of local municipalities.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Concurred, arguing that the grand jury report did not meet the statutory definition for public release and that due process requires all named but nonindicted individuals criticized in a grand jury report to be given notice and an opportunity to respond.

name: JUSTICE DONOHUE
description: Concurred, argued that a mail-in ballot lacking a secrecy envelope is void and therefore does not count as a 'ballot' that would prevent a voter from having their provisional ballot counted, upholding the right to vote.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Concurred, argued that the constitutional text unambiguously limits the proof/presumption qualifier only to the dangerousness exception, not to the life-offense exception, meaning bail is categorically precluded for life-imprisonment offenses.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE TODD
description: Authored the majority opinion, arguing that Articles of Impeachment became null and void upon the expiration of the 206th Session of the General Assembly because the General Assembly's powers last only for the duration of the session in which those bodies came into being.

name: WECHT
description: Concurred with majority opinion and filed a separate concurring opinion.

name: MUNDY
description: Filed a concurring and dissenting opinion.

name: DOUGHERTY
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this matter.

name: BROBSON
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this matter.

name: DOUGHERTY, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the Galapos' signs were protected pure speech under the Pennsylvania Constitution, and the injunction was an unconstitutional prior restraint because the Oberholzers did not prove a substantial and intolerable invasion of privacy.

name: WECHT, JUSTICE
description: Dissented, argued that the injunction was not a prior restraint and that equity courts have the authority to issue narrow injunctions restricting tortious speech that can withstand strict or intermediate scrutiny.

name: BROBSON, JUSTICE
description: Dissented, argued that trial courts can enjoin residential speech that constitutes a private nuisance and disrupts quiet enjoyment, and that the injunction was content-neutral and narrowly tailored to protect residential privacy.

name: Justice Wecht
description: Dissented, argued that inventory searches violate the Pennsylvania Constitution's privacy protections and the appeal should not have been dismissed.

name: TODD CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Appellee failed to meet his burden to establish that Subchapter H's irrebuttable presumption was constitutionally infirm and that Subchapter H does not constitute criminal punishment.

name: Justice Mundy
description: Concurred, but disagreed with the Majority's conclusion that online registration requirements resemble colonial era shaming punishments, believing this factor should not weigh in favor of finding Subchapter H punitive.

name: Justice Wecht
description: Concurred in the result regarding the irrebuttable presumption doctrine but dissented from the finding that Subchapter H is not punitive, arguing it imposes affirmative disabilities, resembles historical punishment, promotes punitive goals, and is excessive.

name: Justice Donohue
description: Dissented, arguing that the Majority misapplied the irrebuttable presumption doctrine by relying on a single statistical fact and that SORNA's lifetime registration and reporting requirements are punitive and unconstitutional.

name: BROBSON, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the General Assembly never enacted a statute vesting the PUC with legislative authority over gas meter locations in historic districts, meaning no unconstitutional delegation occurred.

name: JUSTICE DONOHUE
description: Concurred, argued that the Commonwealth Court lacked original jurisdiction because the Appellants' claims, though styled as challenging parole eligibility, fundamentally challenge the constitutionality of their life sentences without parole, which must be brought under the PCRA.

name: Justice Wecht
description: Dissented, argued that the majority incorrectly concluded that judgments of sentence prohibit parole and that parole ineligibility is part of the sentence, which he believes is not what the Crimes Code states and could hinder future legislative reforms.

name: The Late Chief Justice Baer
description: Did not participate in the decision of this matter.

name: Justice Brobson
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this matter.

name: WECHT, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Act 47 supersedes the City's Home Rule Charter and the Receiver's modifications were necessary and within statutory authority to address the City's severe financial distress and uncooperative officials.

name: Justice Brobson
description: Concurred, but argued that the Plan should be modified to limit the Receiver's independent authority, as Chapter 7 only empowers the Receiver to require, direct, or order officials to implement the plan, not to implement it independently.

name: Justice Dougherty
description: Dissented, argued that the five challenged modifications are contrary to Act 47 or otherwise unlawful, arbitrary, and exceed the Receiver's authority, thus should have been rejected.

name: TODD, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the legislative process for Act 12 satisfied the "original purpose" and "single subject" mandates of Article III of the Constitution.

name: Justice Dougherty
description: Concurred, argued that the "public health programs" provision fits within the unifying subject of "benefits pertaining to the basic necessities of life to low-income individuals" because the funds are authorized to assure medical assistance recipients have access to healthcare services.

name: Justice Mundy
description: Concurred, argued that Article III, Section 1, is silent on a non-deception requirement for a bill's title, and the court should adhere to the plain text of the Constitution.

name: Justice Donohue
description: Dissented, argued that Act 12 violates both the "original purpose" rule and the "single subject" rule, and the majority's holding condones logrolling.

name: Justice Wecht
description: Dissented, argued that Act 12 was enacted in violation of the Pennsylvania Constitution because the court's case law undermines the constitutional mandate for transparent and orderly legislative processes, particularly regarding omnibus bills and logrolling.

name: BAER, C.J.
description: Did not participate in the decision of this matter.

name: Justice Brobson
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this matter.

name: DONOHUE, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the General Assembly intended to give the Agencies leeway to promulgate the challenged regulations, which are reasonable and fall within the ERA's conception of "public resources."

name: DOUGHERTY, JUSTICE
description: Concurred that Agencies did not exceed rulemaking power for "other critical communities" but dissented regarding "common areas of a school's property," "playgrounds," and "playground owners" as public resources, arguing the Agencies exceeded their authority based on ejusdem generis analysis.

name: WECHT, JUSTICE
description: Concurred with the reversal of the Commonwealth Court's order for most definitions but dissented regarding "other critical communities" and the PNDI database, finding a fatal procedural defect in its incorporation without formal rulemaking.

name: MUNDY, JUSTICE
description: Dissented, arguing the Agencies exceeded their statutory authority in promulgating the challenged regulations and that the PNDI receipt requirements violate the Documents Law.

name: JUSTICE DOUGHERTY
description: Concurred, argued that the school district's selective property assessment method is not uniform or neutral and is unreasonably discriminatory, especially due to outdated county-wide assessments.

name: Justice Donohue
description: Concurred with Justice Dougherty's opinion in support of reversal.

name: JUSTICE DONOHUE
description: Concurred, argued that Act 77's universal mail-in voting provisions are constitutional and previous interpretations of "offer to vote" were flawed.

name: JUSTICE WECHT
description: Concurred, but disagreed with the determination that Act 77 prescribed an "other method" of voting under Article VII, Section 4.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Dissented, argued that the state Constitution requires in-person voting by default and Act 77 is unconstitutional.

name: JUSTICE BROBSON
description: Dissented, argued the majority overruled 160 years of precedent without sufficient justification.

name: BAER, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that PEDF failed to prove the challenged provisions violate the Pennsylvania Constitution, as the use of funds for DCNR's operations and statewide environmental projects, and Lease Fund changes, align with trustee duties under the ERA.

name: SAYLOR
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this matter.

name: TODD
description: Concurred, joined the majority opinion and Justice Donohue's concurring opinion.

name: DONOHUE
description: Concurred, argued that while concerns exist about non-trust use of assets, the facial challenge fails, and detailed accounting will allow for future as-applied challenges.

name: DOUGHERTY
description: Dissented, argued that the challenged appropriations and fiscal code sections are facially unconstitutional for permitting non-trust use of funds and commingling without proper accounting, violating ERA trustee duties.

name: WECHT
description: Dissented, argued that the upheld legislation is facially unconstitutional due to allowing non-trust use of trust corpus and commingling without transparent accounting, similar to previously struck-down provisions.

name: MUNDY
description: Concurred, argued that the Commonwealth's allocation of oil and gas lease funds for broader trust purposes, beyond just remediation, is consistent with its trustee duties under the ERA.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Concurred, arguing that the warrantless seizure of blood was not justified by exigent circumstances because the blood was already drawn and preserved, and the constitutionality of the implied consent statute (Section 3755) did not need to be addressed.

name: JUSTICE WECHT
description: Concurred that exigent circumstances were absent but dissented from the Majority's avoidance of the constitutional question, arguing that the implied consent statute (Section 3755) is unconstitutional.

name: Justice Donohue
description: Concurred with Justice Wecht's opinion, arguing that exigent circumstances were absent and the implied consent statute (Section 3755) is unconstitutional.

name: Justice Dougherty
description: Concurred with Justice Wecht's opinion, arguing that exigent circumstances were absent and the implied consent statute (Section 3755) is unconstitutional.

name: TODD, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Appellant's claims based on incorrect legal advice regarding the settlement's consequences are not barred by Muhammad, and her fraud claim can proceed.

name: SAYLOR, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this matter.

name: WECHT, JUSTICE
description: Concurred in the result, but argued that the Muhammad precedent should be overturned entirely as it is deeply flawed and unjust.

name: MUNDY, JUSTICE
description: Concurred in the result, and agreed with Justice Wecht that the Muhammad rule should be disapproved and that the present dispute offers a convenient vehicle to do so.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE BAER
description: Concurred, argued that a Batson violation, while reprehensible and warranting a new trial, does not constitute the most egregious prosecutorial misconduct that would bar retrial under Pennsylvania's Double Jeopardy Clause, as it was not a tactic designed to provoke a mistrial or intentionally deprive the defendant of a fair trial.

name: Justice Mundy
description: Concurred, argued that the established remedy for a Batson violation has always been a new trial, and the expansion of double jeopardy protections in *Johnson* does not change this, as Batson violations are a distinct type of violation not to be commingled with other prosecutorial misconduct analyses for double jeopardy.

name: Justice Donohue
description: Dissented, argued that all Batson violations, as intentional acts of racial discrimination, inherently constitute prosecutorial overreaching that fundamentally breaks down the judicial process and should always result in the dismissal of charges (barring retrial) under Pennsylvania's Double Jeopardy Clause.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE BAER
description: Concurred, argued that the smell of marijuana alone is not sufficient to establish probable cause for a warrantless vehicle search, but can be a factor in the totality of circumstances.

name: Justice Saylor
description: Concurred, argued that the suppression court's ruling was based on expert testimony that the smell of legal and illegal marijuana is indistinguishable, and did not support broader pronouncements.

name: Justice Dougherty
description: Concurred that marijuana smell is a factor but not stand-alone probable cause, but dissented from reinstating the trial court's suppression order, arguing for remand to consider other factors.

name: Justice Mundy
description: Concurred that marijuana smell is a factor but not stand-alone probable cause, but dissented from the application of that holding to the facts, arguing the trial court overlooked relevant factors.

name: JUSTICE DONOHUE
description: Concurred, argued that DHS failed to establish probable cause for a home inspection, violating Fourth Amendment and state constitutional rights by applying a diluted standard.

name: JUSTICE DOUGHERTY
description: Concurred in the result that DHS lacked probable cause but dissented from the majority's analysis, arguing it made pronouncements on child welfare law not necessary for the case and that the probable cause standard for child protection differs from criminal law.

name: Justice Todd
description: Concurred in the result that DHS lacked probable cause but dissented from the majority's analysis, arguing it made pronouncements on child welfare law not necessary for the case and that the probable cause standard for child protection differs from criminal law.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Dissented, argued that DHS established sufficient probable cause for the home inspection, and that the trial court should be permitted to consider all information, including prior involvement and anonymous reports, given the distinct nature of child protective investigations.

name: JUSTICE WECHT
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court committed an error of law in denying bail without proper evidentiary hearing, but this error was harmless and did not affect the trial outcome, and that text message screenshots were admissible as duplicates under the best-evidence rule.

name: BAER, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the 'substantially more likely than not' standard for denying bail adopted by the Majority is substantially identical to the 'clear and convincing evidence' standard and should be applied.

name: TODD, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Commonwealth sufficiently proved that only incarceration would assure public safety, agreeing with the outcome regardless of the standard of proof.

name: MUNDY, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Majority inappropriately heightened the Commonwealth's burden of proof for denying bail and that the 'substantially more likely than not' standard is contrary to precedent.

name: Justice Todd
description: Concurred, authored the majority opinion, arguing the Victim's Rights Amendment violated the separate vote requirement by combining multiple, non-interrelated changes that substantively altered existing constitutional provisions.

name: Justice Mundy
description: Dissented, arguing the proposed amendment was properly submitted as a single ballot question because its changes were narrowly tailored to a singular objective of victims' rights and did not substantively alter other existing constitutional provisions.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Concurred, argued that an order denying summary judgment based on sovereign immunity is a collateral order appealable as of right because sovereign immunity protects government entities from suit, and this protection is irreparably lost if appellate review is postponed until final judgment.

name: DOUGHERTY
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this matter.

name: JUSTICE DONOHUE
description: Concurred, argued that bonus payments, rentals, and late fees are income but must be returned to the trust corpus because the ERA does not create income entitlements for beneficiaries.

name: BAER, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that Section 27 should not be subject to intricate private trust principles but rather general trust concepts, and questioned whether the ERA was intended to govern income from natural resources.

name: SAYLOR, J.
description: Dissented, argued that applying private trust law principles to a public trust is incongruous and favored the narrowest application possible, affirming the Commonwealth Court's rationale.

name: WECHT
description: Concurred, argued that the ERA creates a trust where natural resources are the corpus, the Commonwealth is the trustee, and the people are beneficiaries, and revenue from trust asset sales cannot be redirected to the General Fund.

name: MUNDY
description: Concurred with the majority's analysis of bonus, rental, and late fees as income, but dissented on the analysis of Article I Section 27, aligning more closely with the Commonwealth Court's view.

name: JUSTICE WECHT
description: Concurred, argued that the sentencing statute is unconstitutionally vague because it fails to specify a maximum term, violating due process, and the judiciary cannot infer a maximum term.

name: SAYLOR, J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that the sentencing statute is not unconstitutionally vague as a six-month maximum can be inferred from constitutional norms for summary offenses, and the judiciary should not declare it vague based on the majority's reasoning.

name: JUSTICE DONOHUE
description: Concurred, argued that the death penalty is constitutional and that Hairston's counsel was not ineffective regarding the verdict slip, prosecutorial conduct, or expert testimony.

name: JUSTICE SAYLOR
description: Concurred, expressed concerns about the prosecutor's use of misleading language regarding aggravating factors and the scope of expert testimony, but ultimately concurred in the result.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE SAYLOR
description: Concurred, argued that an unreasonably delayed license suspension, through no fault of the driver, can deny due process, and the source of the delay (PennDOT or court clerk) is immaterial.

name: JUSTICE WECHT
description: Concurred in the result but dissented from the majority's reasoning, arguing that the Vehicle Code itself, not due process, should provide the remedy for judicial delay, and that the clerk's failure to report should invalidate the suspension.

name: Justice Todd
description: Concurred in the result but dissented from the majority's reasoning, arguing that the Vehicle Code itself, not due process, should provide the remedy for judicial delay, and that the clerk's failure to report should invalidate the suspension.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Dissented, arguing that the Gingrich framework should be overruled, that only PennDOT's delay should be a basis for relief, and that the driver could have mitigated prejudice by inquiring about the suspension status.
